{"class": "fixable",
 "chokepoint": [{"operator": "page reads through the asynchronous I/O layer", "component": "asynchronous I/O layer", "frozen": true,
   "why_every_version_executes_it": "A full scan of orders for LIKE '%qz%' must read every orders table page. No index can serve a leading-wildcard pattern.",
   "least_work": {"amount": 4394, "unit": "pages", "per_unit_cost_us": 1.0,
     "total_ms": 4.4, "calling_context": "warm OS page cache, each page read once, batched reads"},
   "max_cores": 1}],
 "floor_ms": 4.4, "L_delta": -4.02,
 "rationale": "The frozen I/O floor is about 4.4 ms (assumed ~1 µs per page), far below T_R_upper of 245.9 ms. About 61% of Turso's 3.7G instructions are in exec_like, which is mutable VDBE code. Fix: compile the pattern once per statement and turn '%lit%' into a memchr/memmem substring search, as SQLite does with strcspn. That would close the gap. Start-up adds only about 4 ms."}
